component_findings.publish_version: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--kotlin): Kotlin does not have a single unified, mature package manager independent of the JVM build-tool ecosystem (unlike e.g. Cargo or npm as a single canonical tool); its package-management strength is substantially inherited from Gradle/Maven/Maven Central rather than being a Kotlin-native invention, and multiplatform-specific dependency/publishing tooling is documented as still maturing (legacy-mode deprecation warnings, Alpha-stage unified toolchain publishing).
component_findings.registry_security: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--kotlin): Kotlin officially supports both Gradle (with a dedicated Kotlin DSL) and Maven as first-party build/dependency-management systems.
component_findings.resolver_lock: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--kotlin): Kotlin dependency resolution defaults to Maven Central, giving it access to the entire mature JVM package ecosystem shared with Java/Scala/Groovy.
component_findings.workspace_multi: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--kotlin): Kotlin dependency resolution defaults to Maven Central, giving it access to the entire mature JVM package ecosystem shared with Java/Scala/Groovy.

metric.package_dependency_management_qua.limitations: Kotlin does not have a single unified, mature package manager independent of the JVM build-tool ecosystem (unlike e.g. Cargo or npm as a single canonical tool); its package-management strength is substantially inherited from Gradle/Maven/Maven Central rather than being a Kotlin-native invention, and multiplatform-specific dependency/publishing tooling is documented as still maturing (legacy-mode deprecation warnings, Alpha-stage unified toolchain publishing).
metric.package_dependency_management_qua.selection_rule: Evaluate the standard/de-facto package workflow using official documentation and current registry/tool behavior; ecosystem size is scored elsewhere.
